title: Woods's partner frozen at the wheel
place_text: Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota

tellings.quote: I even tried pulling his hand off that steering wheel.
I could not figure out what was happening and turned to look at ------- and saw that both his hands were on the steering wheel and he was looking straight ahead with a blank stare on his face.

plain: During the 1977 night at a South Dakota missile site, the Air Force security guard Mario Woods says his partner sat frozen at the wheel of their truck, and Woods could not bring him round. Woods tells Michels he was there, and says: "I even tried pulling his hand off that steering wheel." He names a man called Michael Johnson in this telling. Woods had described the same moment years before in a written account published by the journalist Robert Hastings on 10 September 2017. There he writes that he "could not figure out what was happening" and turned to his partner, whose name is blanked out in the text, and "saw that both his hands were on the steering wheel and he was looking straight ahead with a blank stare on his face." The 2017 version has the blank stare. The later one adds Woods physically trying to free his partner's hand. If it happened, it would mean whatever came near the truck could freeze a man in place.
